newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain Treasury promoted new 18-mo bills with yield.
newsitem.headline: Spain Treasury promoted new 18-mo bills with yield.

text.p: Spain's 18-month Treasury bills were allotted on Monday at a slighter higher-than-expected yield, as the Treasury decided to sell a relatively big chunk of paper at their debut, dealers said after the auction.
"The Treasury gave a premium in yield term to establish this maturity in the market," said Alfredo Urrutia, chief economist of Societe Generale en Madrid.

The 18-month bill yields made their debut at 5.352 percent on Monday. That compares with grey-market prices of between 5.25 and 5.32 percent earlier on Monday, and dealers expectations at around 5.31/32 percent on Friday.

The Treasury, which sold more than 412 billion pesetas in the first and second rounds of the allocation, wanted the new instrument to stop the slide in the average life of its debt and help it cope with competition from other sovereign issuers.

But the new maturity also well pleased the fast-growing industry of investments trusts, and especially FIAMMs, funds which invest in fixed-rate public and private paper, with maturities of up to 18 months.

"We can say the auction was a success. The Treasury met its target to increase debt life, and at the same time pleased the investment trusts," said Valentin Fernandez, economist at Credit Lyonnais in Madrid.
The advent of the new instrument should allow the Treasury to sell more debt, particularly helpful as it contends with high maturing debt of 5.13 trillion pesetas in June and July.

"We clearly saw the Treasury's intention to establish 18-month-bills well. In June and July it will have to replace more than five trillion pesetas. Of course they won't put everything in 18-month bills, but the new instrument will give same relief," said Urrutia.
Analysts added that these new 18-month bills are likely to replace the investors' and Treasury's preference for the six-month bills.
